analysis:
Examined all supplied metadata, patches and documentation excerpts against the canonical definition index and selected T-041 detail. Changes document a 60-second session-based backoff reset and randomized 0–1-second reconnect after coordinator close code 1012 (changelog.d/provider-fast-reconnect.md:3–5; docs/architecture/components/provider.md:119–143; docs/provider/cli-reference.md head patch:1937–1940). No executable implementation is supplied in this batch, and no concrete security regression is established by these documentation changes.
The surrounding architecture retains fresh socket nonces, teardown of resume state, custody-only endpoint resumption, cancellation of disconnected requests and origin-bound Apple replies (provider.md:108–117,145–150), consistent with TB-002/TB-011, T-010 and T-053. Faster reconnection is not described as authorization or extension of Apple proof lifetime. No changed behavior affecting plaintext encryption, key persistence, cache isolation, build qualification, fan authority or billing is evidenced; existing surrounding claims are not independently revalidated.
Integration should verify CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift, CoordinatorClientState.swift and CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift implement the documented timing and close-code semantics, associate recorded close codes with the originating socket, preserve teardown/cancellation and grant invalidation before replacement, and retain ordinary backoff on failed attempts. Assess repeated 1012 closes and restart-induced registration load for availability; a trusted coordinator's restart hint alone does not establish an adversarial bypass. Implementation correctness remains a material coverage limit, not an observed missing control.
